teaser: How the Web Summit team works with agents: a session per agent, a conductor first, narrow roles, a folder, a key, and coordination as the work.
core_idea: For a team of seven people and soon a hundred agents, an agent is a Claude Code session with a thread, files, a repository and a schedule. Everyone starts with a conductor that coordinates their other agents, and every agent gets the narrowest role that makes sense, a behaviour policy and a folder in the repository that holds its memory, so sessions are replaceable. Each agent publishes a public key by push, signs what it publishes, and receives secrets sealed to it as QR codes. Humans give direction and pruning, and because the team breaks every team-size rule, coordination is the work.

nodes.label: Woken on a schedule
nodes.summary: A chat becomes a team member.

quotes.text: The history matters less than you would think; the folder is the memory.
Each agent was following its rules.
We work in the future, within the limits of the platforms we have now.
